title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; the compact harmful-change mapping and per-episode traces required to reproduce that preregistered aggregation are archived and their locations are given in Methods. We present the preregistered primary inference, document the absent preregistered safety aggregation, and provide exact artifact pointers for reproducible recomputation.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to an LLM repair model. Prior empirical work in program repair and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) demonstrates that verifier-interposed repair can raise verifier-detected pass rates but also introduces risks such as verifier-exploitation and additional interaction costs [1], [2], [3], [4]. Survey and field studies in NetOps warn that read-oriented usefulness does not automatically imply safe closed-loop changes [5].

Motivation, gap, and research question. Systematic controlled-challenge evidence for verifier-guided repair on vendor CLI templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is scarce [1], [2], [5]. An intervention that only activates when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics can be uninformative unless the design ensures activation opportunities. We address that by running a preregistered deterministic controlled-fault injection and a paired design that shares the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair pipelines and verifier-mediated iterative refinement have been evaluated across adjacent domains. Cadenas et al. present controlled generate–verify–repair architectures showing deterministic verifiers improve mechanical pass rates in code/IaC contexts [1]. Recent work applying verifier-first evaluation to IaC and infrastructure synthesis reports improved verifier pass rates when diagnostics guide repair or search [2]. Empirical analyses warn of verifier-exploitation where optimization toward a single proxy verifier degrades true target fidelity [3]. Studies measuring verifier-mediated pipeline costs document a measurable "verifier tax" (increased interaction steps and resource use) that affects operational tradeoffs [4]. Surveys and demonstration-case work in NetOps/AIOps synthesize user-facing benefits and caution about closed-loop automation without robust verification and orchestration [5]. Each cited work is used here for the specific empirical or conceptual claim noted in parentheses: [1] (GVR effectiveness in program/IaC benchmarks), [2] (verifier-first IaC evaluations), [3] (verifier-exploitation demonstrations), [4] (verifier tax and overhead instrumentation), [5] (NetOps survey and field cautionary evidence).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance agreement.

Design and adapter semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index (1..40) one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) was produced and reused across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one shared initial generation and one repair opportunity per condition. Baseline = blind repair (no diagnostics exposed); guarded = repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The adapter-mandated confirmatory task_count = 40; execution completed 39 valid complete pairs (complete_pair_count = 39) and excluded one pair per the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Planned_episode_count = 80; completed_episode_count = 78; failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (maximum_model_calls = 120); source_generation_attempt_count = 40; source_valid_count = 39.

Model sampling and per-call traces (explicit archive pointer). The declared model in the archived configuration is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Per-call sampling parameters and full provider-call traces are archived and auditable: execution/provider_calls/*.json contains the provider-call metadata for each model invocation; execution/execution_log.jsonl contains per-episode call sequencing and timestamps; execution/model_configuration.json records declared runtime settings. Auditors can inspect execution/provider_calls/ and execution/execution_log.jsonl to reconstruct per-call sampling parameters and verify that temperature was unset for the recorded calls.

Scoring rules and harmful-change mapping. Primary success required agreement of deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and simulator-based compliance. The preregistered harmful-change labeling used in the preregistered harmful-overrepair hypothesis is implemented as a frozen transformation artifact (execution/transformation_manifest.json). Compact operational mapping (archived): label an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. Per-episode validator traces with violation codes are archived at execution/scoring/*.json and in execution/raw_results.jsonl and can be used to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation.

Statistical analysis plan. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial). We report discordant-pair counts, the absolute paired risk difference, a two-sided exact p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness rules: primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs per 'complete_pair_primary'; a sensitivity analysis treats missing episodes as failures. Multiplicity: single predefined primary test; subgroup analyses are exploratory.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Run timestamps are in the execution manifest (started_at_utc and completed_at_utc).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507. Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). The analysis artifacts analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv are archived with recorded SHA-256s.

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under the preregistered rule because the source generation was invalid/unscorable (both_missing_pairs = 1). The per-episode terminal error reasons and exclusion records are archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation: status and reproducibility path. The preregistration included a confirmatory safety hypothesis that guarded repair would not increase harmful over-repair beyond a prespecified threshold. The archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired binary result but did not compute that preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). Therefore we do not present a confirmatory harmful-overrepair verdict. The compact harmful-change mapping and per-episode traces required to compute the preregistered aggregation are archived (execution/transformation_manifest.json and execution/scoring/*.json; execution/raw_results.jsonl). Reproduction steps: for each complete pair (analysis/missingness_summary.csv), read validation_after.violation_codes from execution/scoring/<episode>.json, apply the compact mapping (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE → harmful), and compute paired harmful counts and the preregistered paired test per the analysis plan. Because the archived confirmatory executor omitted this aggregation, any recomputed harmful-overrepair numbers are exploratory unless incorporated into the archive following the preregistered pipeline.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-pair scoring artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json). Examples in the archive illustrate how validator diagnostics (violation codes) focus repairs away from protected-interface changes or toward restoring required command sequences; these per-episode traces support a plausible causal pathway from diagnostic exposure to improved verifier outcomes.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The preregistered paired result indicates a substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated success when deterministic diagnostics are exposed to the repair model under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics. The paired design isolates the effect of diagnostic exposure because both arms used the same initial controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets. Per-episode scoring traces in the archive show diagnostics often identify concrete violation classes that the guarded repair used to guide corrective edits.

Safety boundary and unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. Crucially, the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; we therefore treat the preregistered safety aggregation as unresolved in the confirmatory claim while providing exact artifact pointers and the compact harmful-change mapping for reproducible recomputation by auditors.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The verifier-guided workflow improved verifier-defined correctness on the tested controlled faults but requires additional interaction steps: the execution manifest records hosted-model_call_event_count = 118 and stage_counts by phase (valid_source_generation = 40; blind_controlled_fault_repair = 39; validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair = 39). These counts permit exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure but do not by themselves justify deployment-level cost/latency conclusions.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: model sampling parameters were recorded per-call (execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl) and the archived model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (unset); null is not evidence of temperature = 0. Construct validity: primary success depends on verifier+simulator agreement; verifier coverage and simulator fidelity limit the operational meaning of "valid." External validity: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic template-based tasks constrain generalization to diverse vendors, live streams, and other models. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 yields reasonable precision for the observed effect but limits per-fault-class inference; subgroup analyses are exploratory.

Recommendations. Practitioners should (a) ensure verifier coverage for critical safety properties, (b) instrument harmful-change indicators (for example using the preregistered mapping archived here), (c) budget for verifier-mediated call counts and latency, and (d) validate designs under realistic task distributions before deploying closed-loop changes. The artifact bundle contains the traces and transformation manifests needed to reproduce the preregistered safety aggregation and to run follow-up replications.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor and therefore remains unresolved; we supply exact archive locations and the frozen harmful-change mapping to enable deterministic recomputation by auditors. We release the artifact bundle for reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The frozen harmful-change mapping used for the preregistered safety hypothesis is archived (execution/transformation_manifest.json). Per-episode raw traces and provider-call traces required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; execution/provider_calls/*.json). The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.
Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
